newsitem.title: CHINA: Kowloon Motor Bus gets 10-year franchise.
newsitem.headline: Kowloon Motor Bus gets 10-year franchise.

text.p: Hong Kong on Tuesday awarded a new franchise to the Kowloon Motor Bus Company (1933) Ltd (KMB) to operate a public bus service on 368 routes for the period from September 1, 1997 to July 31, 2007.

"Considering that a longer franchise will enable the company to plan ahead and to secure the financial support of the banking sector of its investment, the Chief Executive in Council has approved the grant of a new 10-year franchise to KMB," a government spokesman said.
The new franchise will not be subject to any Profit Control Scheme, and the routes will be specified as non-exclusive.
A mid-term review will be conducted after the fourth year.

The government also conditionally approved KMB's proposal to transfer ownership of its permanent depot site at Lai Chi Kok to a subsidiary, which will lease it back to KMB until a replacement West Kowloon Reclamation site is provided.

The subsidiary will be required to charge a nominal rather than market rent, further disposal by the subsidiary will be restricted, and KMB shareholders will pay for the cost of constructing a modern depot on the West Kowloon Reclamation.
At present, KMB has a fleet of 3700 buses, eight short term tenancy sites and eight permanent sites.
